latin.286:
§. V.
Ut proinde tantum de Veritate Fundamentali intellecta ac exposita locum reperiant quae sub finem Preliminar. Quaestionum ad Declarat. Theol. de Vera August. Conf. estimatione, supra citatus Dn. Hannekenius ita disserit:
latin.287: Non potest esse sana Unio mystici Corporis ejusque membrorum, cum Veritas laeditur: violatur enim protinus Vinculum Unionis, Charitas, quae è Veritate oritur.
latin.288: Vana Charitas est cum laesione Veritatis, inanis Veritas absque exercitio Charitatis. Nemo aperiet veram charitatem sine professione solidâ Veritatis; neque quisquam audiet Confessor fidelis salutaris doctrinae, qui ruptâ Charitate scindit Unionem.
latin.289: Conf. 1.Cor. I. 10.seq. II. 12. III. 6. VIII. 9.seq. IX. 27. X. 23. 24. 33. 34. XII. 4.seqq. 25.seq. XIII. toto, XIV. 3.seqq. 40. XVI. 13. 14. quam Epistolam finit fortissimo epiphonemate: Si quis Dominum Jesum non amat, qui una est vera Salus est, Salutaris Veritas, sit anathema, Maranatha.
latin.290: Ita ponens in Cognitione Veritatis salutem, ut amandum Jesum doceat, qui in Synaxi Unionis non potest adamari.
latin.291: Pestilens Charitas est absque Veritate, & maledicta omnis Ecclesiastica Unio, quae Jesum non amat in Veritate: 1.Joh. IV. 10. 11. 12.seq. pag. m. 39. Confer Tractatulum nost. Germanicum: Kurzer Entwurff der Einigkeit der Evangelisch-Lutherischen und Reformirten. §. 4. à pag. 21. ad 25.

pass_a.286: §. V. Accordingly, only concerning Fundamental Truth understood and set forth do those remarks find a place which, toward the end of the Preliminary Questions on the Theological Declaration concerning a True Estimate of the Augsburg Confession, the above-cited Hannekenius discusses thus:
pass_a.287: There cannot be a sound Union of the mystical Body and its members when Truth is wounded: for at once the Bond of Union is violated — Charity, which arises from Truth.
pass_a.288: Vain is Charity with injury to Truth; empty is Truth without the exercise of Charity. No one will show true charity without solid profession of Truth; nor will anyone hear a faithful Confessor of saving doctrine who, charity having been broken, splits the Union.
pass_a.289: Compare 1 Corinthians 1:10ff.; 2:12; 3:6; 8:9ff.; 9:27; 10:23–24, 33–34; 12:4ff., 25f.; 13 entire; 14:3ff., 40; 16:13–14 — which Epistle he closes with the strongest epiphonema: If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus, who alone is true Salvation, saving Truth, let him be anathema, Maranatha.
pass_a.290: Thus placing salvation in the Knowledge of Truth, so that he teaches Jesus must be loved — who cannot be deeply loved in a Synaxis of Union [that is ruptured].
pass_a.291: Pestilent is Charity without Truth, and cursed is every Ecclesiastical Union that does not love Jesus in Truth: 1 John 4:10–12ff., page m. 39. Compare our German tract: Short Sketch of the Unity of the Evangelical-Lutheran and Reformed. §. 4, from page 21 to 25.

286: §. V. So those remarks apply only where Fundamental Truth is understood and laid out.
Toward the end of the Preliminary Questions on the Theological Declaration for a true estimate of the Augsburg Confession, Hannekenius (cited above) treats the point this way:
287: Wound Truth, and the mystical Body with its members cannot stay in sound union.
Charity — the very bond of that union — is violated the moment it loses the Truth from which it springs.
288: Charity with injury to Truth is vain; Truth without the exercise of Charity is empty.
No one shows true charity without a solid profession of Truth.
Nor is anyone heard as a faithful confessor of saving doctrine who, having broken Charity, splits the Union.
289: He points to a long run of 1 Corinthians (chs. 1–3, 8–10, 12–14, and 16:13–14).
The letter’s strongest closing cry is: anyone who does not love the Lord Jesus — the one true Salvation and saving Truth — is anathema, Maranatha.
290: On that reading, salvation sits in knowing the Truth, and that knowledge teaches us to love Jesus.
Where the synaxis of union is already torn, that love cannot go deep.
291: Charity without Truth is pestilent, and every church union that does not love Jesus in Truth is cursed (1 John 4:10–12ff., p. m. 39).
Compare our German tract: Short Sketch of the Unity of the Evangelical-Lutheran and Reformed, §. 4, pages 21–25.
Stop before §. VI (limits of Consociation considered formally — Tolerance vs perfect Union).
